title: Registry Run Key Modification (Persistence)
exclusions: Reports observed value changes under the machine and per-user `Run`/`RunOnce` registry locations documented by Microsoft, including their 32-bit `Wow6432Node` views, from either Sysmon event 13 or native Security event 4657. It does not cover Startup folders, `Policies\Explorer\Run`, `RunServices`, StartupApproved state, Winlogon, Active Setup, services, scheduled tasks, WMI subscriptions, browser extensions, other autostart extensibility points, registry key creation/deletion/rename, or execution of the configured command. Sysmon 13 identifies a value-set operation but Microsoft documents complete written-value capture only for DWORD/QWORD; `Details` must not be assumed to contain a complete string command on every Sysmon/schema version. Event 4657 exists only when Audit Registry Success and a matching Set Value SACL are effective; per-user hive coverage must be managed for each profile. Sysmon and 4657 have different field and coverage contracts, and a duplicate observation is not automatically two changes. The result does not prove persistence, execution, malicious intent, authorization, complete endpoint/profile coverage, current registry state, or regulatory compliance. The catalogue search contains no threat-intelligence verdict or exception lookup.
evidence: After deployment, retain the version-controlled `windows_run_runonce_value_changes` saved-search definition, ACL, schedule, dispatch and triggered-alert history; each result with endpoint, telemetry source, registry key/value, operation, process path/ID/GUID when supplied, actor context, old/new or Sysmon detail values, event-record ID, source, and event time; and a protected drilldown or immutable export of the matching raw event. Retain the approved Sysmon binary/version and configuration hash, Sysmon service/config event evidence, effective Sysmon Operational input, or—when using 4657—the effective Audit Registry policy, exact Run/RunOnce SACLs for machine and user hives, and Security input. Also retain endpoint/profile inventory, source-health and field-quality results, `reg query`, Registry Editor, or PowerShell current-state comparison, process/sign-in correlation, approved-change or incident disposition, bounded notification exceptions, and dated positive/negative controls. These artifacts demonstrate what configured telemetry and Splunk reported. This documentation-only review generated no registry mutation, Sysmon or Security event, Splunk result, alert, persistence execution, or production evidence and does not establish complete collection or causality.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In an isolated test index and fixed UTC interval, replay (1) one XML Sysmon event 13 with `TargetObject=HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\UC129Test`, `EventType=SetValue`, distinct `Image`, `ProcessGuid`, `ProcessId`, `User`, `Details`, `Computer`, and `EventRecordID`; and (2) one XML Security event 4657 with `ObjectName=\REGISTRY\USER\S-1-5-21-111-222-333-1107\Software\Wow6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce`, `ObjectValueName=UC129AuditTest`, distinct Subject, `ProcessName`, `ProcessId`, `OperationType`, old/new values, computer, and record ID. Run a copy of the primary SPL with only the index changed. Expect exactly two rows, `telemetry_source=sysmon_13` and `security_4657`, correct normalized key/value/process/actor fields, and no conflation of Sysmon `Details` with Security `NewValue` provenance.
controlTest.negativeScenario: In a separate interval, replay Sysmon event 12 and 14 records at the positive Run path, Sysmon 13 records under `RunServices`, `Policies\Explorer\Run`, and `Explorer\StartupApproved\Run`, a Security 4657 under an unrelated registry key, a Sysmon 13 under the Security source, and a valid-source record missing endpoint or value name. Expect zero rows. Then replay the same logical value set through both Sysmon 13 and Security 4657 and confirm the base search returns two source-labelled observations; any event-level reconciliation or exact time-bounded change-ticket exception belongs downstream and must not erase either raw record.

dataSources: Two explicit XML Windows Event Log paths feed `index=wineventlog`. Preferred rich telemetry: Microsoft Sysmon event 13 (`RegistryEvent` value set) from `source=XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational`, `sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog`, after a Sysmon RegistryEvent configuration includes the in-scope Run/RunOnce paths; required fields are `EventCode`, `EventType`, `TargetObject`, `Image`, `ProcessGuid`, `ProcessId`, `User`, `Details`, `Computer`, and `EventRecordID`. Native alternative or corroboration: Microsoft-Windows-Security-Auditing event 4657 from `source=XmlWinEventLog:Security`, the same source type, after `Object Access > Audit Registry` Success and Set Value SACLs are applied to every in-scope machine/user key; required fields are `ObjectName`, `ObjectValueName`, `OperationType`, `SubjectUserName`, `SubjectUserSid`, `SubjectLogonId`, `ProcessName`, `ProcessId`, `OldValue`, `NewValue`, `Computer`, and `EventRecordID`. Collection is event-driven via WinEventLog inputs, not an API, HEC, script, or modular-input poll.
app: Splunk Add-on for Sysmon (`Splunk_TA_microsoft_sysmon`, Splunkbase 5709) 5.0.1 or a later compatible release for Sysmon input/field/CIM knowledge, plus Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (`Splunk_TA_windows`, Splunkbase 742) 8.1.2 or a later compatible release for XML Windows event handling and native Security events. Install collection configuration on endpoints or a dedicated WEC and deploy parsing/search-time knowledge to the tiers required by the topology. Qualify the exact Sysmon, Windows, forwarder, add-on, CIM, and Splunk platform versions. No premium app is required for the raw rule.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog ((source="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=13) OR (source="XmlWinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4657))
| eval telemetry_source=if(EventCode=13,"sysmon_13","security_4657"), endpoint=coalesce(Computer,ComputerName,dest,host), raw_registry_path=if(EventCode=13,TargetObject,ObjectName), registry_key=if(EventCode=13,replace(TargetObject,"\\[^\\]+$",""),ObjectName), value_name=if(EventCode=13,replace(TargetObject,"^.*\\",""),ObjectValueName)
| eval registry_key_lc=lower(registry_key), registry_key_lc=replace(registry_key_lc,"^\\registry\\machine","hklm"), registry_key_lc=replace(registry_key_lc,"^\\registry\\user","hku")
| eval relative_key=replace(registry_key_lc,"^(hklm|hku\\[^\\]+)\\","")
| where match(registry_key_lc,"^(hklm|hku\\[^\\]+)\\") AND relative_key IN ("software\\microsoft\\windows\\currentversion\\run","software\\microsoft\\windows\\currentversion\\runonce","software\\wow6432node\\microsoft\\windows\\currentversion\\run","software\\wow6432node\\microsoft\\windows\\currentversion\\runonce") AND isnotnull(endpoint) AND len(trim(endpoint))>0 AND isnotnull(value_name) AND len(trim(value_name))>0
| eval operation=coalesce(EventType,OperationType,"value_change"), process_path=coalesce(Image,ProcessName), process_id=ProcessId, process_guid=if(EventCode=13,ProcessGuid,null()), actor=if(EventCode=13,coalesce(User,"UNKNOWN"),coalesce(SubjectUserName,"UNKNOWN")), actor_sid=if(EventCode=4657,SubjectUserSid,null()), actor_logon_id=if(EventCode=4657,SubjectLogonId,null()), old_value=if(EventCode=4657,OldValue,null()), observed_new_value=if(EventCode=13,Details,NewValue), observed_value_type=if(EventCode=4657,NewValueType,null()), event_record_id=coalesce(EventRecordID,RecordNumber), input_source=source
| table _time endpoint telemetry_source operation registry_key value_name process_path process_id process_guid actor actor_sid actor_logon_id old_value observed_new_value observed_value_type event_record_id input_source
| sort 0 - _time
description: Reports value-set observations at Microsoft Windows machine and per-user Run/RunOnce autostart keys, including 32-bit redirected views, from Sysmon event 13 or native Security event 4657. It normalizes registry key and value identity while preserving the telemetry source's distinct process, actor, old/new-value, and event-record semantics.
value: Run and RunOnce values can launch software when a user signs in, so an unexpected write can establish persistence or create reliability and support risk. Source-labelled, process-aware evidence lets responders compare the change with software deployment and current state without overstating a registry write as confirmed execution or malware, and the native-audit branch provides a controlled option where Sysmon is unavailable.
implementation: Choose and document the source contract: configure Sysmon RegistryEvent collection for the exact Run/RunOnce paths and collect its Operational channel with the Sysmon and Windows add-ons, or enable Audit Registry Success plus Set Value SACLs on every in-scope machine/user key and collect Security event 4657. Validate profile coverage, field extraction, event identity, and duplicate paths; then save `windows_run_runonce_value_changes`, schedule it every five minutes over a delayed window, and review every base result before applying exact expiring notification exceptions.
visualization: Lead with expected-endpoint/profile source health and separate Sysmon versus 4657 coverage. Show a newest-first table with endpoint, telemetry source, operation, registry key/value, process, actor context, old/new or Sysmon detail value, event-record ID, and raw drilldown; add a 24-hour timeline, 30-day counts by key/value/process, and panels for missing process/actor/value detail. Correlate to current Registry Editor or PowerShell state and approved software/change records. Never label the written command as executed solely from this event.
cimSpl:
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where (Registry.registry_path="*\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run*" OR Registry.registry_path="*\\Wow6432Node\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run*") by Registry.action Registry.dest Registry.process_guid Registry.process_id Registry.registry_hive Registry.registry_path Registry.registry_value_data Registry.registry_value_name Registry.registry_value_type Registry.user Registry.vendor_product
| rename Registry.* as *
| eval registry_path_lc=lower(registry_path)
| where match(registry_path_lc,"\\(wow6432node\\)?microsoft\\windows\\currentversion\\run(once)?(\\|$)")
| table firstTime lastTime count action dest process_guid process_id registry_hive registry_path registry_value_name registry_value_data registry_value_type user vendor_product
| sort 0 - lastTime
schema: Microsoft Sysmon event 13 and Windows Security event 4657 raw XML contracts; optional CIM Endpoint.Registry
dataModelAcceleration: Optional for the Sysmon/EDR-normalized branch only. Splunk Add-on for Sysmon maps registry telemetry to the CIM `Endpoint.Registry` dataset, but acceleration must be tested for the installed add-on/CIM versions and may include products or registry actions beyond the raw two-source contract. Compare raw Sysmon 13 records with normalized action, destination, process, hive, path, value name/data/type, user, and vendor product over fixed windows. Security 4657 old/new values and subject/logon semantics are not guaranteed by this aggregate. Keep the raw SPL authoritative for source-specific evidence.

knownFalsePositives:
A source-valid Sysmon 13 or Security 4657 row is evidence of an observed registry value operation, not a false event. False positives arise when downstream handling declares every Run/RunOnce write malicious or assumes the written command executed.

1. **Software installation, update, repair, or uninstall** — Legitimate applications frequently register tray agents, collaboration clients, endpoint products, and update helpers. Match the exact endpoint, key, value name, package identity, signed installer/process evidence, deployment job, and approved interval. Do not allow-list a mutable process path or publisher alone.

2. **Windows component, driver, or user-profile setup** — First logon, profile creation, device installation, and Windows servicing can write RunOnce values to complete setup. Confirm the image/build workflow, user SID/profile, exact value, and expected one-time lifecycle. A RunOnce value that persists or is recreated remains reviewable.

3. **Endpoint management, security, VPN, backup, or remote-support agents** — Managed tools can maintain autostart values. Require a version-controlled baseline by value name/path/data and a deployment record. Unexpected command data, process, user, endpoint, or timing must not inherit the exception.

4. **Group Policy Preferences, configuration management, or remediation scripts** — Central automation can enforce registry values repeatedly. Correlate the policy/job ID, target collection, actor/process, and desired value. Do not suppress every event from PowerShell, `reg.exe`, SYSTEM, or a management account.

5. **Administrator troubleshooting or incident response** — An administrator may create, modify, or remove a startup value under a ticket, including containment of a malicious value. Preserve the change as evidence and require the exact endpoint, value, action, owner, and bounded interval.

6. **Approved red-team, Atomic Red Team, or control-test activity** — T1547.001 tests intentionally write Run keys. Require named operators, test assets/values, UTC start/end, and exercise ID. Keep raw events and test results; suppress notification only for that bounded scope.

7. **Sysmon and Security dual collection of one logical operation** — The same write can produce one event 13 and one 4657. This is corroboration, not necessarily duplicate ingestion. Reconcile by endpoint, registry key/value, process ID, actor, and tight event time while preserving both source records. Do not use a broad `dedup` that hides repeated writes.

8. **Duplicate forwarding or replay** — Local plus WEF collection, checkpoint reset, or fixture replay can duplicate the same source event. Compare originating computer, channel, EventRecordID, `_raw`, and `_indextime`; repair collection ownership rather than suppressing by key or process.

9. **Common signed binary writing an unusual command** — `msiexec.exe`, `reg.exe`, PowerShell, an updater, or a signed vendor process can be abused. Process reputation alone is insufficient. Inspect command data, signer/hash from separate process telemetry, parent process, user/logon, destination, and change context.

**Safe suppression:** leave `windows_run_runonce_value_changes` unfiltered. Apply a version-controlled `windows_run_key_change_exceptions.csv` only in downstream notification, keyed narrowly by endpoint or governed asset group, normalized key, value name, telemetry source if necessary, approved value pattern/hash, process, owner, ticket, numeric `valid_from`, and `valid_until`. Reject wildcard keys, actor-only or process-only matches, open-ended dates, and exceptions that discard raw events. Log and review all suppressed observations.
hardware: In-scope Microsoft Windows client and server endpoints whose Run/RunOnce machine and loaded user hives are covered by Sysmon RegistryEvent rules, native Audit Registry SACLs, or both. Sysmon must be installed and running for event 13; native 4657 requires no Sysmon but does require effective audit policy and per-key SACL coverage. Offline/unloaded profiles and non-Windows autostart mechanisms are outside this implementation.
reviewer: documentation-only editorial review against Microsoft Run/RunOnce, Audit Registry/event 4657, Sysinternals Sysmon/event 13, Splunk Add-on for Sysmon and Microsoft Windows, CIM Endpoint.Registry, Splunk Security Content, and MITRE ATT&CK sources; no registry write, Sysmon configuration, SACL/audit-policy deployment, fixture replay, SPL/CIM execution, alert delivery, production validation, or Microsoft/Sysmon/Splunk/endpoint-security SME runtime sign-off

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites, key scope, and source choice

Assign Windows endpoint, identity/profile, Sysmon, audit-policy, Splunk collection, detection-content, software-deployment, and response owners. Define endpoint and user-profile coverage before enabling alerts. Microsoft documents four primary autostart keys: `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run`, machine `RunOnce`, `HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run`, and user `RunOnce`. This rule also includes 32-bit redirected `Software\Wow6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run` and `RunOnce` views. It intentionally excludes adjacent persistence locations so its evidence and false-positive policy remain reviewable.

Choose Sysmon 13, native Security 4657, or both. Sysmon 13 supplies `Image`, `ProcessGuid`, `ProcessId`, `User`, `TargetObject`, and `Details`, but Microsoft describes it as a Registry value-set event and guarantees the written value in the event for DWORD/QWORD types; validate string-detail behavior on the exact Sysmon schema/version. Security 4657 supplies Subject/logon, process, object/value, operation, and old/new-value fields, but only when **Object Access > Audit Registry** Success and a matching **Set Value** SACL are effective. Audit policy without the SACL produces no 4657. A SACL on one user's loaded hive does not prove all current/future profiles are covered.

Install and pin a supported Sysmon release when using event 13. Install Splunk Add-on for Sysmon 5.0.1 or a later compatible release and Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows 8.1.2 or later on the topology tiers required by their documentation. Verify package provenance, deployment ownership, Windows/forwarder/add-on/CIM/Splunk compatibility, and rollback. This editorial review did not execute a runtime matrix, so no `splunkVersions` field is asserted. Search roles need read access to `index=wineventlog`; raw registry values, account/SID data, paths, and process context require restricted access.

## Step 1 — Configure Sysmon and/or native Audit Registry collection

For Sysmon, start from a reviewed organization configuration, not an unfiltered default. Include RegistryEvent paths precisely and preserve the configuration hash. A representative fragment is:

```xml
<Sysmon schemaversion="4.90">
  <EventFiltering>
    <RuleGroup name="UC-1.2.29 Run and RunOnce" groupRelation="or">
      <RegistryEvent onmatch="include">
        <TargetObject condition="contains">\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\</TargetObject>
        <TargetObject condition="contains">\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce\</TargetObject>
        <TargetObject condition="contains">\Software\Wow6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\</TargetObject>
        <TargetObject condition="contains">\Software\Wow6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce\</TargetObject>
      </RegistryEvent>
    </RuleGroup>
  </EventFiltering>
</Sysmon>
```

Use the schema version accepted by the installed Sysmon binary; the fragment is illustrative and must be merged with the full reviewed configuration. Install or update through the organization's software-control process, for example `sysmon64.exe -accepteula -i <config>` for initial lab installation and `sysmon64.exe -c <config>` for a controlled update. Confirm the active configuration with the supported Sysmon command, Sysmon service state, and Sysmon Operational configuration events. The `RegistryEvent` filter can generate event IDs 12–14 for included paths; this UC deliberately selects only event 13 value-set records.

Collect the local channel as XML with a deployment-app stanza such as:

```ini
[WinEventLog://Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational]
disabled = 0
renderXml = true
current_only = 0
index = wineventlog
source = XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational
```

Verify the winning input with `splunk btool inputs list WinEventLog://Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational --debug`. Current Splunk Add-on for Sysmon documentation identifies `XmlWinEventLog` as the source type; channel identity belongs in `source`. Do not force the obsolete channel-qualified value into `sourcetype`. For WEF/WEC, use the add-on's dedicated collector-channel guidance, preserve original `Computer`, and validate latency/duplication before using the direct-source SPL unchanged.

For the native branch, enable Audit Registry Success through controlled Advanced Audit Policy and verify with `auditpol /get /subcategory:"Registry"` or the locale-appropriate GUID/name. Apply Set Value auditing SACLs to each exact machine key and every in-scope loaded user hive through supported Registry Editor, GPO registry security, or endpoint-management policy. Document inheritance, principal, access mask, profile creation/loading, and rollback. Broad registry SACLs can create high volume; do not audit the entire registry merely for this UC. Collect `[WinEventLog://Security]` with `renderXml=true` into the same index and verify `source=XmlWinEventLog:Security`, `sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog`.

Maintain separate source-health reports. For Sysmon, check expected service/config state, Operational-channel freshness, event IDs, source metadata, and endpoint identity. For 4657, reconcile endpoint/profile/key SACL inventory, effective audit policy, broad Security-channel health, and field extraction. Zero Run-key events is not a heartbeat. If both paths are enabled, preserve each raw record; one logical write can legitimately emit two differently identified events.

## Step 2 — Save, schedule, and understand the source-labelled search

Save the sidecar SPL as `windows_run_runonce_value_changes`. Schedule every five minutes over a measured delayed interval such as `earliest=-10m@m latest=-1m@m`; trigger on any result. The first clause enforces exactly two supported XML source contracts. It does not accept an EventCode under the wrong channel. `telemetry_source` prevents analysts from confusing Sysmon's process-oriented payload with Security's audited Subject/old/new-value payload.

For Sysmon, `TargetObject` includes the value name, so `replace` separates the final component from the key. For 4657, `ObjectName` and `ObjectValueName` are already separate. The next stage lowercases only a comparison copy, maps native `\REGISTRY\MACHINE`/`\REGISTRY\USER` roots to Sysmon-style `hklm`/`hku`, strips the exact machine or user-SID hive prefix, and then permits only four relative paths: native and 32-bit Run/RunOnce. This exact comparison prevents a broad `*CurrentVersion\Run*` wildcard from silently including RunServices, Policies, StartupApproved, or similarly named keys.

The output retains the original `registry_key` spelling. `operation` preserves Sysmon `EventType` or Security `OperationType`; operation labels can be localized or rendered codes, so the search does not fabricate one taxonomy. `process_path` chooses the source-specific image/name; actor uses Sysmon User or Security Subject only within that source; Security old/new values and Sysmon Details remain visibly source-labelled. A missing endpoint or value name violates the evidence contract and is dropped into a separate field-quality report. One row is an observation, not proof of persistence or execution.

Do not deduplicate Sysmon against 4657 in the base search. Build optional downstream reconciliation only after proving a key of endpoint, normalized key/value, process ID, user, and a narrow time tolerance; process IDs can be reused, clocks can differ, and two rapid writes can be real. Keep both raw event-record IDs. Apply bounded exceptions only in a notification copy and preserve exception metadata.

The optional `cimSpl` follows Splunk's `Endpoint.Registry` dataset and Splunk Security Content's registry-field contract. Before enabling acceleration, verify that the installed Sysmon add-on maps the raw event to `action`, `dest`, process GUID/ID, hive/path, value name/data/type, user, and vendor product. The post-`tstats` regex narrows a broad indexed path predicate back to exact Run/RunOnce boundaries. Compare raw and CIM rows over fixed intervals. The CIM result may include other EDR vendors and does not guarantee Security 4657 Subject/logon or old/new-value semantics; it is a normalized analytic, not an evidentiary replacement.

## Step 3 — Validate source semantics, paths, and controls

Run both `controlTest` scenarios in isolated indexes and absolute time windows. Assert the two positive source labels and every normalized field. Confirm the native user path becomes an `hku`-scoped comparison while the displayed original remains intact. Assert that event IDs 12/14, wrong sources, malformed records, and adjacent keys return zero. Add positive cases for machine/user native and Wow6432Node Run and RunOnce paths, plus negative prefix/suffix lookalikes. Test blank Sysmon Details and Security old/new values without substituting one source's meaning for the other.

For a safe live lab control, use a disposable endpoint/profile and a harmless non-executed marker or lab binary under endpoint-owner approval. Create an exact value, then change it so value-set telemetry exists, for example through `reg.exe` or PowerShell; remove it after preserving evidence. Do not use production Run keys solely to test detection. Compare with the Registry Editor interface and Event Viewer at **Applications and Services Logs > Microsoft > Windows > Sysmon > Operational** or **Windows Logs > Security**. Match endpoint, source, EventCode, UTC time, key/value, process, actor where supplied, old/new/detail semantics, and EventRecordID. Query current state with `reg query` or `Get-ItemProperty`; current absence does not invalidate a historical write.

For Sysmon, verify the active configuration actually includes the path and compare event 13 with nearby process event 1 by ProcessGuid. For 4657, disable either Success auditing or the key's Set Value SACL in a controlled variant and confirm Windows does not produce the expected event; restore both and retest. Test machine and at least two user profiles, including newly provisioned profiles, to expose SACL coverage gaps. Validate WEF original-computer identity, forwarder restart/checkpoint continuity, duplicate routes, late events, XML field extraction, access controls, and source-health alerts.

Record exact Windows/Sysmon/add-on/forwarder/CIM/Splunk versions, configuration and fixture hashes, audit policy/SACL state, test account/profile, commands, UTC bounds, expected/actual rows, raw record IDs, search job, current-state comparison, failures, and approver. Keep `status=draft` until both selected source branches, endpoint/profile coverage, alert delivery, dashboard, exceptions, and response receive runtime and SME acceptance.

## Step 4 — Operationalize triage, response, dashboard, and evidence

Place source health and profile/SACL coverage before detection counts. Build the source-labelled table and trends in `visualization`; expose the original raw event and current-state query. Separate “observed writes” from “confirmed unauthorized persistence.” Restrict raw value data and identity context to appropriate endpoint/security roles, and redact sensitive command arguments from broad dashboards while preserving controlled evidence.

The response runbook should: (1) verify the source event and endpoint/profile identity; (2) identify exact key, value, operation, process, actor, and event record; (3) obtain current value and determine machine versus user and 32/64-bit view; (4) correlate Sysmon process GUID or Security process ID/logon ID with process creation, parent, signer/hash, command line, logon, EDR, package, and management telemetry; (5) compare software inventory, deployment/GPO/configuration jobs, baseline, and ticket; (6) determine whether the value executed at a later sign-in using separate process/logon evidence; and (7) document authorized, benign-but-unexpected, telemetry artifact, control test, or suspicious disposition.

ATT&CK T1547.001 is appropriate when corroboration supports use of the value for boot/logon autostart persistence. A write by itself is not proof of adversary behavior. Prioritize suspicious writable-user paths, unusual command locations, encoded/script interpreters, unsigned payloads, unexpected users/processes, broad fleet changes, values recreated after removal, and changes near other compromise evidence—but calculate that risk downstream and preserve the raw report.

Do not automatically delete a value, kill a process, disable an account, isolate a host, or roll back software from this result alone. A legitimate Run/RunOnce value can be required for security software, installation completion, accessibility, or business applications. Preserve the value and process evidence before approved containment. After remediation, verify current state, source health, and subsequent sign-ins; absence of a new event alone does not prove removal or non-execution.

Retain the artifacts named in `evidence` under local retention/privacy policy. The advisory 90-day cost value is not a legal requirement. Revalidate after Sysmon/config/schema, Windows, add-on/CIM, forwarder, XML rendering, WEF, audit-policy/SACL, profile-management, index, or software-deployment changes.

## Step 5 — Troubleshoot source-specific failures

- **No Sysmon events for a known value set:** confirm Sysmon service/version, active configuration and schema, exact RegistryEvent path condition, Sysmon Operational event locally, WinEventLog stanza, source/source type, checkpoint, index route, and time window. A config file on disk is not proof it is active.
- **Event 13 exists locally but fields are null in Splunk:** verify XML rendering, `source=XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational`, `sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog`, the current Sysmon and Windows add-ons on required tiers, event boundaries, and conflicting props/transforms.
- **No 4657 during a known write:** verify Audit Registry Success and the exact key's Set Value SACL for the writing principal. Check the correct 32/64-bit and user-SID hive. Audit policy alone is insufficient.
- **Machine keys work but HKCU is missing:** map HKCU to the loaded `HKEY_USERS\<SID>` hive, inspect that profile's SACL and inheritance, then check how new profiles receive policy. Do not claim user coverage from one test account.
- **RunServices or StartupApproved appears:** inspect normalized `relative_key` and local modifications to the SPL. The supplied exact `IN` list excludes those paths; a broad wildcard reintroduced scope drift.
- **Sysmon Details does not show the command:** expected for data types/versions outside Microsoft's documented DWORD/QWORD guarantee. Use Security 4657 `NewValue`, a controlled current-state query, or validated EDR telemetry; do not relabel missing Details as complete value data.
- **The same write appears twice:** determine whether it is one Sysmon plus one 4657 observation or duplicate collection of the same source event. Preserve cross-source corroboration; use computer/channel/EventRecordID to diagnose true replay.
- **Actor differs between sources:** Sysmon User is process context and 4657 Subject is the audited requester. Correlate process GUID/ID and logon ID; do not overwrite one with the other or call either a human without identity evidence.
- **CIM tstats is empty or differs from raw:** inspect Endpoint.Registry tags, fields, add-on/CIM versions, acceleration status/range, summaries-only lag, vendor coverage, and exact path normalization. Keep raw source-labelled results authoritative.
- **Alert volume spikes after software rollout:** identify exact values/processes/deployment jobs, keep base telemetry, and add narrow expiring downstream exceptions. Never suppress all SYSTEM, `msiexec.exe`, PowerShell, `reg.exe`, or all writes from Program Files.
grandmaExplanation: We watch the Windows places that tell programs to start when someone signs in. A change there deserves a check because it may be a normal installer or an unwanted program trying to return later, and the record alone does not prove the program actually ran.
